title: FICO’s Monopoly is Fading & Consumers Are the Winners w/ Kelsey Zhu | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 59

metadata.title: FICO’s Monopoly is Fading & Consumers Are the Winners w/ Kelsey Zhu | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 59

summary: Kelsey Zhu explains how lender choice and price differences threaten FICO's mortgage franchise. Eisman maintains his short and sketches a conditional further 40% fall; Zhu projects multi-year share and earnings pressure. They then compare information-services business models, including data networks, recurring revenue, customer demand and AI exposure. Subsequent VantageScore usage supports the competitive direction, while precise share targets and long-term AI outcomes remain open.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Eisman asks questions, discloses his short and gives the closing synthesis. Kelsey Zhu gives the sector analysis and formal analyst forecasts. Attribution follows turn-taking; guest ratings are not Eisman positions.
framework_points: Trace the distribution chain and distinguish algorithm ownership from underlying data.
Compare complete pricing schedules and funded-loan denominators, not headline fees alone.
Separate earnings risk from multiple compression.
Distinguish shared sector labels from actual end-market exposures.
Eisman remains cautious on software until evidence of AI effects accumulates.
tools_and_charts: FICO per-pull versus success-fee pricing arithmetic
Moat source, management, capital allocation and balance-sheet capacity
transcript_cautions: Captions alternate 10C and 10T; context clearly identifies FICO Score 10T.
Eisman briefly states $4.95 for 10T and is immediately corrected to $0.99; the corrected schedule is retained.
Validation and implementation are conflated in one guest statement.
Hour-format timestamps are included through the final 1:10:53 disclaimer.

claims.claim: FICO 10T is about ten times as expensive as VantageScore after success fees, even with only 15%-30% of applications closing.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Specify pulls per application, bureau count, score fees per funded borrower and close rate. With one score per application, 0.99 + 65c equals $10.74 at c=.15 and $20.49 at c=.30; repeated pulls change the average.
claims.reason: The fee arithmetic can create a large premium under simplified assumptions, but a universal tenfold comparison does not follow without consistent denominators.
